decisions.mark: describes the external bridge's two-level thread structure: one accept thread that spawns a further thread per connected client
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`ExternalBridge::accept_loop` | `external_bridge.cpp:796` (from `start`) | Polls the listen fd every 500 ms, checks peer uid, and spawns one serve thread per client." and "Per-client serve thread (`ct->thread`) | `external_bridge.cpp:945` | Runs `serve_client`" | WHY: The answer states that the accept thread spawns one serve thread per client, which is the two-level structure. || QUOTE: "`ExternalBridge::accept_loop` | `external_bridge.cpp:796` (from `start`) | Polls the listen fd every 500 ms, checks peer uid, and spawns one serve thread per client." and "Per-client serve thread (`ct->thread`) | `external_bridge.cpp:945` | Runs `serve_client`" | WHY: The answer states an accept-loop thread that spawns one serve thread per connected client, which is the two-level structure. || QUOTE: "`ExternalBridge::accept_loop` | `external_bridge.cpp:796` (from `start`) | Polls the listen fd every 500 ms, checks peer uid, and spawns one serve thread per client." and "Per-client serve thread (`ct->thread`) | `external_bridge.cpp:945` | Runs `serve_client`" | WHY: The answer states that the accept loop thread spawns one serve thread per connected client, which is the two-level structure.
